articleBlocks: Spring and Tap first made me think about water in general, which was close but still much too broad. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Fountain gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.
Oasis kept the water theme alive, though it still felt more scenic than practical.
Fountain is the clue that changed the board.
Once I read that as drinking fountain, the set stopped being about water imagery and started being about actual places or sources where someone can get a drink.
Spring, Tap, Well, and even Oasis all fit better under that more practical frame.
The answer was Places to get drinking water.
What makes the board work is that every clue touches water, but only one answer explains them as usable sources.
fullAnalysis: Spring and Tap first made me think about water in general, which was close but still much too broad.
Oasis kept the water theme alive, though it still felt more scenic than practical.
Fountain was the turning clue because drinking fountain is a much tighter reading than decorative fountain.
That shift changes how the whole board behaves. Spring, Tap, Well, and Oasis all stop being water-related images and start acting like real places or sources where drinking water can be found.
The answer was Places to get drinking water.
The puzzle becomes much cleaner once the board is read through access and source rather than through water as a loose topic.
solutionNarrative: Spring and Tap gave me the broad water theme immediately, but not the exact category. Oasis made the board feel even wider because it could belong to scenery, travel, or desert geography.

Fountain narrowed it. Once drinking fountain came to mind, the answer became about where people actually get water, and the earlier clues all re-read as practical sources rather than as general water imagery.
